answer: An agent market can require each identity to lock funds for 90 days, with its share of paid tasks proportional to its stake. This stake-weighted trellis lets new agents bridge the trust canyon without letting extra names create extra earning power: splitting $1,000 among a thousand identities yields the same total task share as staking it once. To gain more access, an attacker must lock more capital and bear its financing cost for the full term.
